reviewed.review: Dammit, this is still great. It still actually looks really good, which is especially hard considering the era it was made in, which was the early digital transition — there are a lot of things from that era that end up looking pretty trashy. Fabulous opening, too. It's a great episode, a great piece of Kon's work. And it's always interesting to see someone who primarily works in one medium translate to another — in this case, a film director going and doing a 13-episode TV series. So I'm very happy that we're watching/reviewing this again, and I'm definitely looking forward to seeing where this crazy show goes, one I haven't watched in over 20 years.

I finally watched an episode of this, so this is an out-of-order review. S-tier. It's fabulous. At least episode one was incredible—so well done, one of those things where you watch it and you're like, "yeah, just make good anime and everything in the world will be better."
This is a show I still fondly remember watching quite a few times and would be happy to go back to.

What I would say is good here is the OST, the OP, and the overall animation quality. The first half of the first season is pretty fun, but that's like ~6 eps. The second half of the first season gets less good. Then there's eps 13-24 of season 1; boy, just terrible. The animation was still good, but it went into such weird story stuff and totally lost me. Then there's every season after that, which was just worse. So I'll give it a 3, splitting a 5 for the first few eps and a 1 for everything after that. I'm sure I'm being too kind to this show, but I'm a bit of a softie.

Plenty of good reasons this show is critically loved and very popular.
OMG. This show is nuts, brutal.

I started and stopped several times. I was coerced by my bestie because she loves it. She’s also 13.

I think the show itself is (at least up to ep 18) a shallow clone of Naruto, but without some of the charm and innocence.

It’s exceedingly well produced by the A-Team at MAPPA. But I don’t care about it that much. I’d rather read Naruto or watch MHA (My Hero Academia).

Or read / watch Chainsawman if you want the same MAT (MAPPA A-Team).

So, is it bad? No. Do I care about it and what happens? Not really. But at least it looks nice and has some fun fights.

However, OMG it suffers so much from the modern Shonen Jump problem where they have to have all these terms and abilities and all this stuff built and expositioned so much. Think back to the beginnings of Naruto - it stays simple for many volumes and gradually adds to the complexity of the rules and world and ninja mechanics.

CSM does go a bit deeper in the modern SJ over depth but… that one is so much more about the characters and they are just more fun.

I’ve been told that “it gets good in season2!” But I’ve been told that about shows for my entire life (and told others) and you know what? That’s the Origin Story of my VQAR (very quick anime reviews). No, you don’t get 10 hours to “get good”. Just be good from the start.

And an addendum: I have now watched up through ep ~40. It's still exceedingly well produced, animated, drawn. I still don't really understand the world, but at least it looks nice.
